text:
maya: heads-up — we're seeing a p99 jump in euw-a10 after the rollout that started ~08:00 UTC. impact mostly generation routes, short chat prompts (<=128 tokens).
jonathan: saw that on graphs, p50 unchanged but p99 doubled. any obvious noisy-neighbor / infra chatter?
lukas: nothing on host-level metrics, NIC rx/tx flat. queue depths went up briefly. Profiling suggests a hot path in kernel selector when seq_len <= 128.
maya: exact numbers: baseline p99 ~120ms, current ~260-300ms. RPS same. KV cache hit-rate on those routes dropped from 78% -> 52% during spike.
sre-jen: CI perf flagged this morning too — job perf/latency-e2e failed in euw-a10 matrix, link: https://ci.company.internal/1755 (perf diff attached).
maya: i'm starting a bisect against recent merges. suspicious merge: #3782 (kernel selection heuristics + fallback ordering). pinging @jonathan who reviewed.
jonathan: I remember changing weight logic to prefer the new fused kernel for short sequences, but added a safety fallback. Could fallback be slower path being chosen erroneously? :thinking_face:
lukas: dump from runtime logs around selection decisions (sanitized):
```
2026-03-17T08:03:12Z selector: model=redwood-v2 seq=64 hw=A10 candidate_order=[fused_v2, fallback_scalar, fallback_tiled]
2026-03-17T08:03:12Z selector: chosen=fallback_scalar reason=perf_estimate_conflict
2026-03-17T08:03:12Z executor: kernel=fallback_scalar exec_time=2.34ms token
```
l ukas: (typo above) but we see fallback_scalar chosen frequently even when fused_v2 should be faster per offline bench.
sre-jen: also relevant: KV cache eviction spikes coincide with the selection changes — could be memory footprint difference between kernels causing more KV spills?
maya: good call. I profiled memory working set: fused_v2 uses ~1.2GB less per device for kv caching on L4/H100 profiles but on A10 the fused implementation maps to a tiled fallback that increases per-request KV allocations.
jonathan: hmm A10 driver/kernel constraints — perhaps the fused path ended up using a vendor kernel that's not available on some A10 SKU, leading selector to pick scalar fallback. Merge 3782 added a heuristic that prefers fused if hardware_capability_flag exists; maybe flag detection is flaky.
ops-bot: deploy: rollout started by canaryer/auto at 2026-03-17T07:50Z, 12/120 shards updated.
maya: timeline: canary shards saw spike immediately after their update, so rollout is the vector. We should hold/revert.
lukas: bisect results (quick):
- revert candidate: revert 3782 -> latency returns to normal on a canary (manual test).
- revert 3778 (other) -> no change.
So 3782 strongly implicated.
jonathan: I can prepare an emergency revert PR. If we revert, we should also gate selection heuristic with an explicit A10 SKU whitelist until we root cause.
sre-jen: agree. We also need to add a CI matrix test for short-seq p99 on A10 in perf-e2e to catch this next time. The current matrix misses kernel variation.
maya: can we patch selector to fall back to previous deterministic ordering for A10s as a quick fix (no codegen changes)? That should be low-risk.
jonathan: yes, will open PR with fallback pin + feature flag disabled by default for legacy A10. target: 30m.
ops-bot: revert requested by jonathan at 2026-03-17T08:22Z.
deploy-bot: revert PR #3794 opened and queued. Status: blocked by presubmit flaky on infra-tests.
sre-jen: okay, if presubmit blocks, can we manually revert the canary via orchestration? We should stop rollout to remaining shards.
maya: stop rollout in console done (paused). We still need to drain canaries or roll them back to previous image. I'll coordinate with infra to roll back 12 canaries.
lukas: also anything we can instrument quickly? Suggest adding a selector telemetry flag that logs (tagged) chosen kernel + perf_estimate vs observed latency for a sample of requests. Will help tune heuristics.
jonathan: adding that to PR too.
maya: next actions summary — jonathan open revert PR + pin A10 fallback, luka s add extra telemetry, sre-jen add ci matrix test, ops pause rollout (done), infra rollback canaries. If revert lands, unpause after verification.
sre-jen: recording incident note in #incidents after revert. Will include perf graphs, bisect steps, and remediation.
maya: thanks all. will update when canary rollback completes. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: action: rollback canaries requested at 2026-03-17T08:28Z (ticket #INC-4829).
maya: rollback finished at ~2026-03-17T08:45Z, preliminary p99 back to baseline on rolled-back hosts. Leaving this thread open for follow-up on CI+telemetry tasks.
